newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria's Assad says Israeli attack "a possiblity".
newsitem.headline: Syria's Assad says Israeli attack "a possiblity".

text.p: Syrian President Hafez al-Assad said on Monday he did not rule out the possibility of an Israeli attack against Syria or Lebanon.

Asked at a joint news conference with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak whether he ruled out an Israeli attack against Syria or south Lebanon, Assad said: "This should not happen, but nobody could say that it will not happen. It is a possibility."
Assad praised efforts exerted by U.S. President Bill Clinton to advance the Arab-Israeli peace talks but added that the process was slowed by the U.S. presidential election campaign.
Tension between Israel and Syria has risen since the election of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in May. Netanyahu has refused to trade occupied Arab land for peace.
Syrian troop movements in Lebanon, where it has 35,000 soldiers, in recent weeks have caused war jitters in Israel. Damascus said the movements were defensive.

Five years of peace talks between the two countries are stuck over the Golan Heights, captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 Middle East War. Israeli talks with Lebanon, where Syria is the main power broker, are dependent on progress on the Syrian front.
